name: United States
note: United States additions to the ITU Region 2 plan - only allocations that are specifically American, or narrower or wider than the Region 2 allocation, are listed here; everything else comes from the base plan. Sources, all primary: 47 CFR 97.301 and 97.303(h) (amateur bands and the 60 m channels); 47 CFR 95.563, 95.963, 95.1763 and 95.2763 (FRS, CB, GMRS and MURS channel tables); 47 CFR 90.531 (700 MHz public safety band plan) and 90.19 (the FirstNet 758-769/788-799 MHz licence); 47 CFR 90.613, 90.617 (Public Safety Pool 806-816/851-861 MHz), 90.16 and 90.621(g) (NPSPAC 806-809/851-854 MHz); 47 CFR 90.35(b)(3) for the railroad-coordinated (LR) VHF channels, whose 160.215-161.565 MHz span is corroborated by NTIA Report 99-370, which describes 181 frequencies spaced every 7.5 kHz from 160.215 to 161.565 MHz; the non-Federal and Federal columns of the FCC Online Table of Frequency Allocations, 47 CFR 2.106, https://transition.fcc.gov/oet/spectrum/table/fcctable.pdf, including footnotes G27 and G30 for the military UHF and VHF bands; 47 CFR 15.247, 15.403 and 15.407 (unlicensed and U-NII), with the U-NII-1 to U-NII-8 labels taken from FCC 20-164 and the FCC 6 GHz fact sheet DOC-407628A1; 47 CFR 18.301 (ISM); 47 CFR 80.371 and 80.373 (marine VHF channels); and NOAA at https://www.weather.gov/nwr/ for the weather radio channels. Two points worth stating because they are commonly got wrong: the US amateur 40 m band is the FULL Region 2 allocation, 7000-7300 kHz, not a narrower slice, so it is not repeated here; and the US 1.25 m band is 222-225 MHz plus a secondary 219-220 MHz segment, which is NARROWER than the Region 2 allocation of 220-225 MHz. The 470-512 MHz T-Band is deliberately NOT drawn: 47 CFR 2.106 footnote NG66 makes it land mobile only in thirteen named urbanized areas and it is television everywhere else. Channel groups (CB, FRS/GMRS, MURS, weather radio) are drawn from the lowest to the highest channel CENTRE frequency, so the outermost half channel falls outside the block; single channels are drawn at their centre plus and minus half the authorised bandwidth. INFORMATIONAL ONLY - a display aid, not an authoritative or licensing reference. JSON has no comment syntax, so this note lives in the data; the loader ignores unknown keys.
